messages.subject: Survival frailty models in INLA
parts:
Hi!

I am trying to understand how INLA works with survival frailty models. I am running another R-package for frailty models (coxme) for comparison. I find that that the random effects (frailties) estimated by INLA is practically 0, while they are certainly not 0 using coxme (i.e. there is a significant within-subject-variation).

I will post my code and results here for comparison. The data set kidney is available in the survival-package.

My questions are:
1. Why does INLA fit an intercept for the Cox model?
2. Why do I get this huge precision for my hyperparameters? (And hence all random effects are 0....)


I am very new to INLA and appreciate any help. I would like to use INLA in my researsch and use both spatial and IID effects, but I get this kinds of results for the IID random effects in all data sets and models that I have tried.

Regards,
Kristin Svenson

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Survival frailty models in INLA
parts:
On Fri, 2015-01-23 at 00:39 -0800, Kristin Svenson wrote:

>
> My questions are:
> 1. Why does INLA fit an intercept for the Cox model?

Hi,

because you asked for it... by default the baseline hazards sums to
zero, hence you need an intercept there unless you say you do not want
the baseline hazard (log-scale) to sum to zero.

> 2. Why do I get this huge precision for my hyperparameters? (And hence
> all random effects are 0....)

this is the default prior which for your case is not what you want. this
one seems more appropriate:

library(INLA)
library(coxme)

f(id,model="iid",
hyper = list(prec = list(param=c(1, 1))))
kid.inla = inla(formula, family="coxph", data=kidney,
control.hazard = list(scale.model = TRUE))
plot(kid.coxme$frail$id, kid.inla$summary.random$id$mean)
abline(a=0,b=1, lwd=3)


assuming an gamma(1,1) prior for that precision, just as an example.

> I am very new to INLA and appreciate any help. I would like to use
> INLA in my researsch and use both spatial and IID effects, but I get
> this kinds of results for the IID random effects in all data sets and
> models that I have tried.
